findings.title: SEAgent guard batch abort mapped as a lost result: 166 never-executed calls in 107 logs; 94 logs get map.missing_tool_result at error severity and index status 'failed' (7 of 200 in L2); the other 13 (only skipped call at batch index 0) get only accounting_inconsistent
findings.evidence: Population (5,342 raw logs, exam-census.json): 960 blocked batches (seagent 575, seagent-RF 385; 0 in other arms), each with exactly 1 call renamed '<tool>BLOCKED_BY_SEAGENT', exactly 1 tool message (answering the renamed call, empty content, error null) and then a user-role guard warning (next role user 960/960; never the last assistant turn). The other calls of the batch get no tool message: 166 calls (seagent 88, seagent-RF 78; 140 after the blocked call, 26 before it) in 107 logs. The family mapper's positional rule (mapper.py _trailing_calls: pending = unlinked and index >= results, not in the last assistant message -> missing_tool_result severity error) flags 94 of the 107 logs (= census 94 = part-A trial 94; 51 seagent, 43 seagent-RF; 84 security, 10 perf; anatomy 'blocked in batch and next message user' 94/94); the 13 logs whose skipped calls all precede the blocked call get only accounting_inconsistent (warning) and seal. Runner (importer.py ~2038) and spec (HL corpus versioning: failed if any issue has severity error) behave as specified, so the 'failed' status and import exit 1 (both j2 wave5 and j1 followup2, failed 7) are consequences, not runner or tool defects. L2: 7 failed = sampled labels among the 94 (mtr_sample.py: 94 / 7); every stage ok; completeness known_incomplete 9 (the 7 + 2 of the 13-class).
findings.hypothesis_ref: H17 (supported as predicted; this finding is the diagnosis), H15
findings.recommendation: Route to the AgentDojo family owner (with D-153): a profile quirk for the SEAgent guard's batch abort (rule citing the renamed call and the following warning) so the skipped calls are recorded as unexecuted calls of a defence intervention (warning, not a declared loss), the same way whether they precede or follow the blocked call. Byte-changing for the 107 logs (AER/SEM/PROV digests, index status, completeness); list it with the regen items and get approval before the round. Until fixed: disclose that the 94 'failed' executions are defence-intervention runs (seagent/seagent-RF) and must not be filtered out of any rate (filtering would be outcome-dependent). Correct the part-A trial note ('a disclosed source fact'): the source shape is real, the error severity is ours. No exclusion.
findings.artefact_proposal: [[artefact]] id = "agentdojo.art.seagent_guard_batch_abort" (proposed): scope.sources = ["seagent-agentdojo"]; description: the SEAgent guard renames one call per batch to '<tool>BLOCKED_BY_SEAGENT', answers it with an empty tool message and drops the batch's other calls before a user-role warning; expected = [{snapshot="seagent-agentdojo:head", count=960, unit="blocked calls"}, {count=166, unit="skipped calls"}, {count=107, unit="logs"}, {count=94, unit="logs with missing_tool_result"}]; recorded_as issues [missing_tool_result, accounting_inconsistent] until the quirk lands
findings.agents_md_12: seagent-agentdojo: the 94 'failed' executions (status) are SEAgent guard batch aborts (166 never-executed calls in 107 logs), not data loss; family quirk routed (PC-01).

verdicts.reasoning: Independent recount (verify/v1.py, own positional rule): 960 blocked batches (seagent 575, seagent-RF/rf 385), 166 skipped calls in 107 logs, 94 logs meet the rule (k >= results, not last assistant); every flagged log has a blocked batch (0 flagged logs without one, 0 unlinked non-final calls in unblocked batches), so the 94 have no other cause. Alternative explanation 'results lost by the logger' tested: 33 of 166 skipped calls are re-issued later with identical function and args, and the blocked call's single tool message is empty (sha256 of empty string, 960/960): consistent with never-executed calls. Not expected-known under R2: D-153 covers only the warnings, the part-A note is a report, not a quirk or decision. Mapped outcomes of the 7 failed units are present (raw = mapped), so no headline change unless status is filtered: S2 holds. Wording fix: skip_pos gives 16 before-only logs; the 13 unflagged logs are those whose only skipped call sits at batch index 0, not 'all skipped calls precede'.

findings.title: The blocked call itself is mapped as an executed tool: 960 '<tool>BLOCKED_BY_SEAGENT' calls become tool_execution status ok with an empty result (41 in the L2 sample); no deny decision
findings.evidence: exam-census.json guard_blocked_batches: 960 blocked calls in 863 logs, each answered by a tool message whose function carries the suffix, error null, content empty (prefix digest e3b0c442... = empty, 960/960). AER of the scratch corpus (dclass.py): tool_execution blocked=True status ok 41, blocked=False ok 691 / error 14 / invalid 3. The tool name is not a benchmark tool; the real tool never ran. The profile header (D-153) routes only the warning message; no rule or quirk mentions the renamed call (grep of src/ and docs/: 0 hits for the suffix). Outcomes are unaffected (AgentDojo scores from environment state).
findings.recommendation: Route with PC-01 and D-153 to the AgentDojo family owner: map the renamed call as a defence deny decision on the original tool (name without the suffix, recorded as such), with the empty tool message as the denial, as interbolt's defence_denial_message rule does; disclose until then that tool-execution counts of the seagent arms include 960 denied calls.
findings.artefact_proposal: part of agentdojo.art.seagent_guard_batch_abort (PC-01): count 960 blocked calls recorded as executions until the quirk lands

verdicts.reasoning: AER of j2: 749 tool_execution records, 41 named '*BLOCKED_BY_SEAGENT' with status ok; record kinds contain no decision record. Profile and mapper have no SEAgent quirk (grep: only the run-dir table, profile, registry mention seagent); precedents rope.art.guard_denial and the interbolt denial quirk show the family maps guard denials, so this is a profile gap, not D-153 scope (D-153 decided the user-role warnings only). Inflates tool-execution counts by 960 and hides a deny decision: must be disclosed, S2.
